conventions.convention: The cycle is the oriented manifold M; the algebra is Ω•(M; C), parity is exterior degree modulo two, and integration extracts and integrates the degree-n component. Berezin integration uses ∫ dθⁿ⋯dθ¹ θ¹⋯θⁿ = 1.
Q is an odd derivation obeying the graded Leibniz rule. S and O are even, V is odd, and Q² need not vanish globally; the required deformation condition is (Q²V)e^(−S−tQV)=0.

Q-invariant integration means IΓ(QF)=0 on the specified admissible class. Zero divergence is a local condition and requires a separate zero boundary or decay flux condition to establish integrated invariance.

The parameter lies in a nonempty open real interval. Complex derivatives use real increments; differentiability holds throughout the interval outside a common null set, and each compact parameter set has one integrable majorant uniform in the parameter.

The theorem concerns finite-dimensional integration at finite parameter values only; it supplies neither a large-parameter saddle-point argument nor an infinite-dimensional continuum functional-integral identity.
The four-torus has periods 2π and orientation dx¹∧dx²∧dx³∧dx⁴; Q=d, O=dx¹∧dx², S=dx³∧dx⁴, and V=sin(x³)dx⁴.

load_bearing.statement: For differential-form integration on an oriented finite-dimensional smooth manifold with positive volume form, let Q be a smooth odd derivation, S and O smooth even forms, V a smooth odd form, and J a nonempty open real interval. Assume QS=QO=0, (Q²V)e^(−S−tQV)=0 and IΓ(Q(OVe^(−S−tQV)))=0 for every t∈J, including the zero-boundary-flux condition. If the top-degree coefficient f_t of Oe^(−S−tQV) is integrable, differentiable in t almost everywhere with measurable derivative, and on every compact K⊂J one integrable majorant bounds both |f_t| and |∂_t f_t| uniformly outside one null set, then Z(t)=IΓ(Oe^(−S−tQV)) is constant on J and Z′(t)=−IΓ(O(QV)e^(−S−tQV))=−IΓ(Q(OVe^(−S−tQV)))=0. No large-parameter saddle-point limit or continuum functional-integral identity is asserted.

Defines integration of smooth complex differential forms by their top-degree component on an oriented finite-dimensional manifold; defines an odd derivation Q, its divergence, an admissible integration class with an explicitly assumed integration-by-parts identity and boundary functional, integrated Q-invariance, and admissible Q-exact deformation data with Q-closure, Q²V, integrability, differentiability and compact-parameter domination conditions.

published_dependencies.used_for: The invariance theorem's F2 and step 2.1: differentiation of the complex integral under a uniform L¹ derivative majorant, applied locally on an open interval inside a compact parameter interval. The cited statement supports this use.
The invariance theorem's F3 and step 4.1: real difference-quotient limits for the real and imaginary components of Z, including the elementary continuity estimate.
The invariance theorem's F4 and step 4.1: each continuous real component with derivative zero on the open interval is constant. The cited statement preserves the interval and continuity hypotheses.

seams_checked.note: The fluctuation-data definition imports the differential-form regulator conventions. The Ward theorem's F3 and proof explicitly match Q-closure, the Q²V condition, integrated Q-invariance, common-null-set differentiability, measurable derivatives and compact-parameter majorants. Regulator existence, continuum integration and the saddle limit remain separate obligations. The supplier asserts no converse or physical regulator construction.

The torus example checks the theorem's algebraic, periodic-boundary and domination hypotheses directly and obtains 4π²λ. The cylinder example computes a nonzero Q-boundary integral and correctly excludes itself from the theorem. Neither example strengthens the supplier into a continuum claim.

The N=2* U(2) regulated Ward theorem separately assumes a finite-dimensional realization of its selected model and all mathematical supplier hypotheses. Its conclusion remains conditional, at fixed regulator, fixed sector and finite parameter; it explicitly excludes saddle limits, ADHM pushforwards, pole matching, regulator removal and continuum measure construction.
